data.body:
Fix pushed: Gerrit change 2590 — https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2590 (commit f118d43d0cfd).

## Option B (batched index), and Option A was killed ON EVIDENCE

The plan-review gate warned that `escaped_defect` is a UNION over all backing reviews, not one ticket per candidate — so 'lazily compile only candidate-referenced tickets' could mean far more tickets than it sounds like. That warning was correct, and measuring it settled the choice:

**The union is 1554 of 1960 review-bearing tickets — 79%.** Option A would have saved about 20%, not three hours. Two places drive it (`fixture_selection.py`): `_fire_rows` does `any(_escaped(r) for r in _unique_reviews(reviews_for_norm))`, and `_no_fire_rows` does `any(_escaped(r) for r in silent)` — where `silent` is EVERY review store-wide that routed the criterion without firing, which is much larger than the candidate set.

So this ticket's own Approach section was wrong about Option A being viable. Recording that rather than leaving the next reader to rediscover it.

Cost of the batched pass: **6.6s** over 6883 ticket dirs (one `reduce_ticket` each; the per-ticket .cache.json makes it cheap) versus the eager reader at a measured **5.17s/call**, so 1554 x 5.17s ~= **2h14m**.

## The actual quadratic, which the ticket did not name

`reducer/_inbound.py::_mentioning_dirs` byte-scans EVERY event file of EVERY ticket per subject, and `show_ticket(include_inbound=True)` calls it once per ticket. That is the O(n^2). `labels.build_escaped_ticket_index` inverts the loop — one pass building both facts instead of n passes each scanning n.

## Byte-identical proof runs the REAL old path

`test_manifest_is_byte_identical_to_the_eager_per_ticket_path` builds a 4-ticket git-backed fixture tracker and runs `select_from_corpus` TWICE: the old side passes `read_ticket_state=labels._read_ticket_state_via_env_override` — the actual callable that used to be the default, not a stub and not a snapshot generated from the new code — and the new side takes the batched default. Both manifests are written and compared byte for byte.

The fixture is non-vacuous: it exercises both escape routes (a story closed `close_class=plan_defect`, and a story named by an inbound `caused_by` from a bug) plus a clean control, so `escaped_defect` genuinely changes ranks. Mutation-checked — breaking the reverse caused_by index made the byte-identical test fail along with three others; restored and re-verified.

Supporting tests: index-vs-real-reader agreement ticket by ticket; `test_default_path_never_compiles_per_ticket_state` (reader monkeypatched to RAISE — the default path never touches it at all, which is stronger than 'only for candidate-referenced'); index built once per run; and a held-out test that both escaped candidates outrank a clean candidate owning the lower uuid tiebreak, with tier and margin equal, so only the escaped-defect sort key explains the order.

## Measured on the real corpus

**74.2s wall** for the whole selection (build_corpus 24.8s, findings load 23.2s, index build 6.6s, select_candidates 14.3s), 25471 rows / 25465 candidates, 2.0 GB peak RSS. Against ~2h15m eager: **~110x**. 4451 of 25465 candidates carry escaped_defect=True, so the signal is live rather than theoretical.

## One deliberate behaviour difference

Where the eager reader RAISED (absent ticket, error/fsck_needed status, no CREATE), the index reports not-escaped instead of aborting the entire selection. This cannot change any row the old path successfully produced, because in that case the old path produced NO rows at all. I checked the skip surface directly: `reduce_ticket` raising still propagates loudly; only a non-dict return is defensively skipped, and absence from the index means NOT escaped — the conservative direction, under-promoting rather than over-promoting.

## Gates

make lint exit 0 (mechanism new=0); make typecheck 750 files; check_complexity_baseline --check new=0 increased=0; targeted suite 243 passed / 3 skipped. fixture_selection.py 491 -> 547 and labels.py 560 -> 614, both well under the 800 cap.

Side benefit worth noting: the batched path avoids `show_ticket` entirely, so it also stops touching the store's freshness/reconverge path — the eager measurement emitted CrossSessionWarning on tickets held by other agent sessions, which this no longer provokes.
